headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Roo Code can overwrite workspace files while gpt-researcher can ingest and emit untrusted content, creating dangerous prompt, conflict, and cascade pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read local documents and uses MCP, while Roo Code can use MCP and operates in a shared VS Code workspace via filesystem. That creates a plausible default bridge where content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not provably blocked, but it is less direct than raw web-to-agent injection.
conditions: IF Roo Code reads gpt-researcher output files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents exchange content through the shared workspace or MCP, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a provenance header to all inter-agent files.
Restrict Roo Code to read-only access on gpt-researcher outputs.
Disable MCP between the two agents for the first run.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Manually review any file before the other agent consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local files and broad network egress is enabled, but Roo Code explicitly shares state via filesystem and gpt-researcher reads local documents and handles API keys. That makes accidental exposure of workspace content or secrets plausible in default use. The profiles do not prove third-party exfiltration of all context, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a workspace containing secrets, those secrets can be exposed to the other agent through shared files.
IF Roo Code writes generated artifacts into the shared workspace, gpt-researcher can read them back.
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate per-agent directories.
Rotate any API keys present in the workspace.
Set file permissions so only one agent can read sensitive files.
Delete generated artifacts after each handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, execute shell, and modify git state; gpt-researcher can read files and spawn subprocesses, and both support multiple instances. Because Roo Code shares state via filesystem and no locking is documented, concurrent edits to the same workspace or repo can corrupt files or git history. This is a default-dangerous overlap with potentially irreversible loss.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same VS Code workspace, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites files while gpt-researcher is generating artifacts, git state can diverge or be lost.
mitigations: Assign separate worktrees.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Disable git writes for one agent.
Use a lock file around shared outputs.
Back up the workspace before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell and git privileges. If Roo Code treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes, commits, or other actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the unsafe default is high.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes gpt-researcher reports without independent verification, incorrect facts can drive actions.
IF gpt-researcher outputs are copied into code or commit messages, downstream automation may amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Require a human review step before actions.
Cross-check claims against source URLs.
Mark research outputs as untrusted by default.
Separate research and execution workspaces.
Disable auto-commit or auto-run on imported text.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and API keys, while Roo Code works inside a VS Code workspace and can write files. If regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, both agents may process it under different retention and logging behaviors. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, both agents may process it under different logging or retention paths.
IF either agent sends workspace content to external model APIs, compliance obligations may differ from local handling.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Use a data-classification checklist before each run.
Disable external API calls for sensitive tasks.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Route regulated workloads to approved systems only.
